eligibility.quote: I just updated my Groovy debian installation with the release that was posted today on ros-users and now collada meshes no longer appear in RViz.  In particular, the TurtleBot is now basically invisible.
eligibility.reason: The concrete rendering regression occurs after upgrading RViz's mesh-loading behavior while retaining a separately supplied model. E1/E4 hold; the mesh unit declaration crosses the model/renderer boundary and the fix changes it, so E2 stops at 6, not deployment wiring. E3 UPGRADE is supported by the reporter.

failed_conditions.reason: The create_body.dae unit declaration changes from centimeters to meters. The resource and unit_mismatch class are directly supported.

supporting_evidence.quote: This patch introduces the ability to read the unit scaling factor from Collada mesh resources.

loudness.quote: Actually, it doesn't look like scaling, but it is pretty messed up on my machine as well (whole robot is just a few speckles of gray and white scattered around)
loudness.reason: The symptom is incorrect visualization. The source shows no diagnostic identifying incompatible units at connection or activation.

detection_stage.quote: In particular, the TurtleBot is now basically invisible.
detection_stage.reason: The failure is observed in the rendered result, not while negotiating a connection.

resolution.quote: turtlebot_create version 2.0.1 fixes this issue. It's now available on shadow-fixed.
resolution.reason: The fix and its model-package release are identified, but the source does not show that released model working in a test with an explicitly identified RViz revision. The earlier successful scale workaround used the commenter's own possibly older meshes. recommended is therefore appropriate.

supporting_evidence.quote: I can't promise that my older meshes are the same as in the newest turtlebot_description package.

notes: The other TurtleBot mesh fixes concern other description packages; they are not additional independent conditions of this selected create_description/RViz composition. The UPGRADE assignment is based on the changed renderer behavior; it is distinct from which side supplies the mesh file's bytes.
